decks.description: “EVERYTHING” is a love song from TEAM BABY. It first came out as a single in 2016, a year before the album. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: The Black Skirts — EVERYTHING

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: The Black Skirts — “EVERYTHING”. A whole world in a room.

Slide 2 of 4. For a song called EVERYTHING, the scene is intimate: two people in a room on a rainy day, with little need to speak. The scale of the declaration comes from how completely that ordinary company fills the speaker’s attention.
slides.text: For a song called EVERYTHING, the scene is intimate: two people in a room on a rainy day, with little need to speak. The scale of the declaration comes from how completely that ordinary company fills the speaker’s attention.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. Affection includes the other person’s less polished moments. There is a fondness for being close enough to see them without ceremony, which gives the repeated declaration its warmth. The lyric makes devotion feel domestic and familiar; very little has to happen for the time together to matter.

decks.description: Here’s “Run with Me” at sunwoojunga’s SERENADE concert, shared on her own channel. The song comes from her 2019 album Serenade; this performance was recorded at Sogang University’s Mary Hall. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: sunwoojunga — Run with Me

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: sunwoojunga — “Run with Me”. Someone who will go with you.

Slide 2 of 4. The invitation to escape comes with room for exhaustion. The person being addressed can cry, move slowly and take the time they need. The speaker offers to accompany them without requiring an explanation of everything that has gone wrong.
slides.text: The invitation to escape comes with room for exhaustion. The person being addressed can cry, move slowly and take the time they need. The speaker offers to accompany them without requiring an explanation of everything that has gone wrong.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. There is also a return in the lyric’s imagined journey. Leaving can be temporary, a pause made possible by someone willing to stay beside you. That gives the reassurance a patient quality: the companion remains present through the difficult part, before anything is fixed.

decks.description: Here’s Car, the garden singing “Tree” for Begin Again’s Open Mic series. The song first came out as a single in April 2019. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: Car, the garden — Tree

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: Car, the garden — “Tree”. Finding room for awkwardness.

Slide 2 of 4. The beloved becomes a dancing tree, and the speaker becomes the rough music within it. The pairing gives awkwardness somewhere to belong. The speaker imagines even their timid fears becoming part of an affectionate picture when they are beside this person.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. Asking for a smile suggests how much that acceptance matters. The lyric treats closeness as permission to bring an uncertain, unpolished self into a relationship. Its tenderness comes from the hope that someone can receive those parts with affection.

decks.description: “Forest” is about feeling small among other people, and finding a place with them. Choi Yu Ree wrote it for her 2022 single release Stroll. This version is from a Bugs-ker live session. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: Choi Yu Ree — Forest

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: Choi Yu Ree — “Forest”. Wanting to be a place for someone.

Slide 2 of 4. The wish to become a forest carries a question about belonging. The speaker wants to offer someone a place to enter and stay, while remaining uneasy about their own place among the trees. A generous wish and a sense of inadequacy occupy the same image.
slides.text: The wish to become a forest carries a question about belonging. The speaker wants to offer someone a place to enter and stay, while remaining uneasy about their own place among the trees. A generous wish and a sense of inadequacy occupy the same image.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. The lyric keeps returning to uncertainty, including whether this place is a forest or a sea. That shifting landscape leaves the speaker’s own position unsettled. Offering shelter does not mean they feel secure themselves; the longing to be recognised remains part of the care they want to give.

decks.description: Ahn Ji-young sings “Eternal love” (사랑할 수밖에) at BOL4’s 2024 Bloom concert in this clip from her own channel. The song is from the 2023 EP Merry Go Round. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: BOL4 — Eternal love

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: BOL4 — “Eternal love”. When love asks for restraint.

Slide 2 of 4. The speaker can only clasp their own hands while watching someone they love from a distance. The gesture holds back a desire to give everything, alongside a fear that their own wants might hurt the person they hope to protect.
slides.text: The speaker can only clasp their own hands while watching someone they love from a distance. The gesture holds back a desire to give everything, alongside a fear that their own wants might hurt the person they hope to protect.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. The devotion in Eternal love includes taking a step back. Its repeated certainty of loving someone sits beside uncertainty about what that love should ask of them. Restraint makes the affection ache: the desire to draw closer persists through the effort to keep it from becoming a burden.

decks.description: “RomanceYouthLove” was one of ESEGYE’s first releases. This recording is from their first BLIND concert at Veloso Hongdae, shared by the band themselves. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: ESEGYE — RomanceYouthLove

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: ESEGYE — “RomanceYouthLove”. Setting off without a destination.

Slide 2 of 4. Romance, youth and love become boats in this song’s central image: things that can carry two people somewhere together. Their destination stays unknown. The repeated reassurance draws its confidence from companionship, even as the lyric admits how little they know.
slides.text: Romance, youth and love become boats in this song’s central image: things that can carry two people somewhere together. Their destination stays unknown. The repeated reassurance draws its confidence from companionship, even as the lyric admits how little they know.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. That admission keeps the optimism a little reckless. Youth appears as a willingness to depart before having an answer, with another person close enough to share the uncertainty. The promise depends on their togetherness; the world ahead has offered no guarantees.

decks.description: “The Wave” keeps going after the last vocal line, with an extended instrumental ending. This version comes from the 2020/NEON concert, filmed at YES24 Live Hall on December 7, 2019. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: SE SO NEON — The Wave

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: SE SO NEON — “The Wave”. A departure with no explanation.

Slide 2 of 4. The Wave gives its brief parting scene a dreamlike strangeness: the departing figure is associated with the moon. There is no explanation of who this person is or what has happened between them and the speaker.
slides.text: The Wave gives its brief parting scene a dreamlike strangeness: the departing figure is associated with the moon. There is no explanation of who this person is or what has happened between them and the speaker.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. That missing context leaves space around the farewell. The lyric holds an image in view without turning it into a complete relationship story, so its emotional distance remains hard to settle. A reading of loss is possible, but the words keep the circumstances open.

decks.description: “ONCE” is about letting someone go while hoping they’ll remember you kindly. Yu Dabin describes that farewell in the band’s release interview for the October 2023 single. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: YdBB — ONCE

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: YdBB — “ONCE”. Hoping to be remembered kindly.
Slide 2 of 4. ONCE looks back at the moment affection began while speaking from the edge of a goodbye. The speaker wants a place in the other person’s memory, even as distance grows between them.
slides.text: ONCE looks back at the moment affection began while speaking from the edge of a goodbye. The speaker wants a place in the other person’s memory, even as distance grows between them.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. That wish gives the farewell its tenderness and its uncertainty: nobody can choose how they will be remembered. Regret remains, alongside a hope that distance need not erase their bond. The song makes room for an attachment that continues as two people grow apart, without promising that affection will bring them back together.

decks.description: WhiteUsedSocks (화이트유즈드삭스): what “Don’t feel sad” is about, in English. One of the band’s early songs. Official recording, release details and sources.
decks.title: WhiteUsedSocks — Don’t feel sad

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: WhiteUsedSocks — “Don’t feel sad”. A wish made through regret.

Slide 2 of 4. Memories arrive before the speaker has chosen to revisit them. The lyric’s wish for the other person to feel less sad is complicated by an admission of having been absorbed in their own feelings. Looking back brings affection and responsibility together.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. That regret changes the force of the title. The reassurance can be heard as a hope for someone’s happiness from someone conscious of their own past selfishness. The wish is modest: to let a memory bring a smile again, even with regret still attached to it.

decks.description: “Don’t run away” was part of the September 2018 soundtrack to A-TEEN. It’s an easy place to meet Motte’s music, even if you’ve never seen the series. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: Motte — Don’t run away

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: Motte — “Don’t run away”. Trust after words go wrong.

Slide 2 of 4. Two people keep trying to get closer and somehow end up further apart. The speaker recognises that their clumsy words have hurt the other person, then asks for the trust that might let them speak more openly.
slides.text: Two people keep trying to get closer and somehow end up further apart. The speaker recognises that their clumsy words have hurt the other person, then asks for the trust that might let them speak more openly.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. There is worry beneath the repeated assurance of mutual belief: the speaker fears being left alone and keeps looking for an answer. Asking about the other person’s day brings the plea down to an ordinary conversation. Repair might begin with hearing what has been difficult, rather than finding a perfect declaration.

decks.description: “Even if you leave” is about the things that are hard to let go of, and the habit of blaming yourself after they’re gone. HANRORO wrote both the words and music. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: HANRORO — Even if you leave

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: HANRORO — “Even if you leave”. The pull of self-blame.

Slide 2 of 4. The Korean title, 자처, carries the sense of bringing something upon oneself. Alongside the English title Even if you leave, it places separation next to responsibility. The speaker’s difficulty letting go becomes tangled with the thought that their pain is their own doing.
slides.text: The Korean title, 자처, carries the sense of bringing something upon oneself. Alongside the English title Even if you leave, it places separation next to responsibility. The speaker’s difficulty letting go becomes tangled with the thought that their pain is their own doing.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. In her release note, HANRORO leaves the addressee open: it could be a person, a past choice or something that traps the self. She describes writing the song to stop feeding self-blame. That context makes the lyric’s guilt a feeling under examination, rather than a verdict that the speaker deserves to suffer.

decks.description: “Someone” holds affection and doubt together. It’s from Kim Sawol’s second album, Romance, released in September 2018. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: Kim Sawol — Someone

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: Kim Sawol — “Someone”. Reassurance with doubt underneath.

Slide 2 of 4. Much of Someone addresses another person as precious and loved. Then the lyric turns towards the speaker’s own lonely night. The confidence of the reassurance becomes more complicated once the person offering it admits feeling unloved.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. That change of perspective leaves tenderness and doubt close together. Being able to recognise someone else’s worth does not make it easy to feel your own. The speaker can offer conviction to another person while still needing to hear something like it themselves.

decks.title: Yerin Baek — 0310

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: Yerin Baek — “0310”. Trying to sound less attached.

Slide 2 of 4. 0310 is sung in English, and its hesitations are part of the story. The speaker tries to sound casual about someone leaving, then admits how much that possibility frightens them. What appears indifferent at first becomes a way of protecting a much stronger attachment.

decks.description: The speaker in “Flower” hoped to bloom, but compares themselves to mold in a damp room. The song pairs that harsh self-image with a wish to keep growing and be loved. This is the official recording from gongwon’s EP 0. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: gongwon — Flower

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: gongwon — “Flower”. Growing in a damp room.

Slide 2 of 4. The official English title is Flower, while 곰팡이 means “mold.” The difference matters to a speaker who expected one kind of growth and sees another in themselves. A damp room gives that disappointment a physical setting: what grows there is shaped by its conditions.

decks.description: In “Only You”, a walk through Seoul Forest brings a changed relationship into focus. The speaker still wants comfort from the person they struggle to face. Yebit sings it here at the Rolling 31st anniversary concert. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: Yebit — Only You

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: Yebit — “Only You”. When the place stays the same.

Slide 2 of 4. Seoul Forest remains familiar while the relationship has changed. Walking there alone makes the difference harder to ignore: a shared place can keep reminding someone of a closeness that no longer feels secure.
slides.text: Seoul Forest remains familiar while the relationship has changed. Walking there alone makes the difference harder to ignore: a shared place can keep reminding someone of a closeness that no longer feels secure.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. The speaker tries to look all right, with a smile that conceals hurt. The person they find painful to face is also the person they want to lean on. That makes the request for comfort unresolved; affection and distress lead back to the same person, and outward composure gives little indication of what remains inside.

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 3. indiek lyric notes: youra — “MIMI”. Calling to someone absent.

decks.description: “Grown Ups” follows someone worn down by the day, wondering whether their small world will ever smile back. Sondia recorded it for the 2018 drama My Mister. This official OST music video uses scenes from the series. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: Sondia — Grown Ups

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 3. indiek lyric notes: Sondia — “Grown Ups”. A question at the end of a long day.

Slide 2 of 3. Among smiling people, the speaker feels like a stranger. Dreams once pursued now seem far away, and the dream of being fully themselves gives way to disappointment on waking. The final question asks whether this small world might someday smile back. It leaves that possibility open, without pretending the sadness has already passed.

decks.description: moneto (모네토): what “She” is about, in English. A wish for memories to remain, like a melody. Official recording, release details and sources.
decks.title: moneto — She (Feat. MRCH)

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 3. indiek lyric notes: moneto — “She (Feat. MRCH)”. Keeping someone’s memories close.

Slide 2 of 3. The woman in the song feels alone even in a crowd. The refrain imagines sleep as a place where she can find the company she misses, then looks ahead to old age and asks that her memories remain. Comparing them to a melody gives that wish a form: something that can return, even when the person is absent. The lyric does not explain exactly why they are apart.

decks.description: An alarm clock, afternoon dessert and a phone before bed become everyday opponents in “Surrender”. MRCH’s song from Oh, Life lets go of the wish to be invincible. This live clip was shared on her own channel before the EP’s release. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: MRCH — Surrender

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 3. indiek lyric notes: MRCH — “Surrender”. Putting down the need to win.

Slide 2 of 3. Battle language gives ordinary distractions an outsized role: an alarm calls, a screen keeps the speaker awake, and a message unsettles them. Waving a white flag means giving up the demand to defeat every one of these small pressures. The wish is modest: some peace and a little fun.

decks.description: In “Old Town”, friends have moved away while the speaker remains. Wanting to leave and wanting to stay keep trading places. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: Say Sue Me — Old Town

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: Say Sue Me — “Old Town”. The places remain, the friends have gone.

Slide 2 of 4. The speaker feels left behind as friends leave town. Each wish to go meets a wish to stay, and the order keeps reversing. Neither choice becomes a settled answer: leaving might change their situation, but attachment to the town remains.
slides.text: The speaker feels left behind as friends leave town. Each wish to go meets a wish to stay, and the order keeps reversing. Neither choice becomes a settled answer: leaving might change their situation, but attachment to the town remains.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. Later, the speaker addresses someone absent, reporting that their familiar street and beach are still there. These ordinary updates make the separation clearer: the places remain available, but spending time there together is no longer possible in the same way. The town still has crowds, yet the speaker feels empty. What is missing is particular company, rather than people in general.

decks.description: “NO PAIN” invites people who have felt excluded into a house where everyone can sing together. The speaker also admits to having thought of leaving and asks not to be hated, keeping that welcome unsettled. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: Silica Gel — NO PAIN

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: Silica Gel — “NO PAIN”. An invitation with room for uncertainty.

Slide 2 of 4. The house the speaker has made offers a concrete place for people who have been excluded. Singing together is the invitation: belonging begins with something they can share. The warmth of a communal fire extends that welcome, giving the gathering a small, tangible centre.
slides.text: The house the speaker has made offers a concrete place for people who have been excluded. Singing together is the invitation: belonging begins with something they can share. The warmth of a communal fire extends that welcome, giving the gathering a small, tangible centre.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. Yet the speaker also says they had thought of leaving that day, and asks not to be hated. Wanting others close does not settle whether the speaker will stay. Later lines set the love of family and others, left in the sun’s keeping, beside vigilantes who gather once the night fog thickens, intending to steal. That threat stands next to the opening welcome, and the lyric does not say how it ends.

decks.description: A falling construction crane makes the possibility of sudden death concrete in “Beep-Boop, Beep-Boop”. The speaker asks why attention should arrive only after someone disappears. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: Meaningful Stone — Beep-Boop, Beep-Boop

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: Meaningful Stone — “Beep-Boop, Beep-Boop”. Being heard before disappearing.

Slide 2 of 4. The imagined crane accident places danger on an ordinary walk. Alongside it, the request against belated phone calls suggests a hurt that already exists: the speaker wants attention while they are still here. People shutting their ears while news grows louder makes public noise feel distant from the person asking to be heard.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. The ending changes the focus from when death might happen to what it should mean for others. Its repeated wishes resist having a death exchanged for another person’s sacrifice, grief, money or reputation. The circumstances remain open, but the repetition gives the speaker a clear boundary within that uncertainty.

decks.description: People seeking food are called witches, rioters and wolves in “There is A Wolf” (늑대가 나타났다). The lyric gives those accused a reply: they are the workers who make the food others enjoy. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: Lang Lee — There is A Wolf

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: Lang Lee — “There is A Wolf”. Who gets called a wolf.

Slide 2 of 4. The closed city gates separate hungry people from the food kept within. As people grieve, demand bread or take grain, threatening labels follow them. The wolf of the title can be read as a name imposed on people whose hunger is treated as a danger, while the conditions behind their actions go unanswered.
slides.text: The closed city gates separate hungry people from the food kept within. As people grieve, demand bread or take grain, threatening labels follow them. The wolf of the title can be read as a name imposed on people whose hunger is treated as a danger, while the conditions behind their actions go unanswered.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. Later, the people being described speak for themselves. They identify themselves as the makers of bread and wine, insisting on their work and their need to feed their children. The speaker’s reference to poor friends also brings the story closer to everyday life. Poverty becomes something the addressee is asked to consider as a possible part of their own future.

decks.description: A conversation with her mother turns Seoul Station into a way of looking back at the speaker’s life: arriving for a university entrance exam, expecting to become a painter and finding a living in music. JEONGMILLA wrote the words and music. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: JEONGMILLA — Departing from Seoul Station

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 5. indiek lyric notes: JEONGMILLA — “Departing from Seoul Station”. The station stays as life changes.

Slide 2 of 5. The song begins with a mother’s practical worries about a late journey home after a performance. The speaker answers with a small reassurance: since moving, she can walk home from the station. That ordinary detail gives the conversation its closeness; there is no grand announcement, just news that might ease a parent’s concern.
slides.text: The song begins with a mother’s practical worries about a late journey home after a performance. slides.altText: Slide 3 of 5. Seoul Station then connects the present to an earlier arrival for a university entrance exam. The speaker once expected to become a painter and now makes a living singing. She acknowledges how often life has changed since she was twenty without deciding whether those changes amount to success or failure.

slides.altText: Slide 4 of 5. The station also offers routes to her hometown and a school friend’s house. It belongs to her relationships as much as her memories. The closing wish to take a train to the sea before summer keeps the future modest and open: another possible departure from a familiar place.

decks.description: “Dancing in the Rain” asks for a hand to hold as the ground collapses. Its Korean title, 춤을 춰요, is an invitation to dance, placing an ordinary gesture of companionship amid destruction. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: Lacuna — Dancing in the Rain

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: Lacuna — “Dancing in the Rain”. Holding on as the ground gives way.

Slide 2 of 4. The speaker finds people difficult to trust but remains willing to love. That willingness first appears in an awkward, ordinary scene: drunken dancing and belongings falling from pockets. The request to take a hand makes closeness possible within that clumsiness.
slides.text: The speaker finds people difficult to trust but remains willing to love. That willingness first appears in an awkward, ordinary scene: drunken dancing and belongings falling from pockets. The request to take a hand makes closeness possible within that clumsiness.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. As the images turn to collapsing ground, cuts and blood, the invitation to dance persists. The speaker’s assurances of being all right sit beside a request for companionship in the present; the danger remains. The closing embrace and movement into a dream can be read as a shared retreat from destruction, though the lyric leaves the pair’s fate unresolved.

decks.description: In “Something’s Wrong”, running between buildings brings the speaker back to the same place. OHCHILL’s album notes say it follows people living day by day in a busy city, including depressed and lost people and young people driven to think about death while pursuing a normal life. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: OHCHILL — Something's Wrong

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: OHCHILL — “Something's Wrong”. Moving without getting anywhere.

Slide 2 of 4. The brightly lit city sits beside an empty room where the speaker is alone. Outside, running through enclosing buildings ends back at the starting point. These images make the frustration concrete: neither staying inside nor moving through the city offers much relief.
slides.text: The brightly lit city sits beside an empty room where the speaker is alone. Outside, running through enclosing buildings ends back at the starting point. These images make the frustration concrete: neither staying inside nor moving through the city offers much relief.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. A string of English words keeps recasting the speaker: liar, runner, loser and, foolishly, only half a fighter. None settles into a secure identity. Against those shifts, the refrain repeatedly objects to a world that allows no difference. By the end, the accusation also includes the world’s dishonesty, but there is no clear escape or resolution. The lyric leaves the speaker’s anger and difficulty speaking side by side.

decks.description: In “Island” (섬), an island exposed to wind and waves becomes a place for feelings the speaker cannot soothe. The song asks whether living with oneself must keep hurting, leaving the question open. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: Kang Asol — Island

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 5. indiek lyric notes: Kang Asol — “Island”. An island without shelter.

Slide 2 of 5. The island offers no refuge: others cannot find or reach it, yet the speaker has nowhere to hide from the cold wind. Waves have swept them there. These details make being alone feel exposed and involuntary, rather than a peaceful retreat.
slides.text: The island offers no refuge: others cannot find or reach it, yet the speaker has nowhere to hide from the cold wind. Waves have swept them there. These details make being alone feel exposed and involuntary, rather than a peaceful retreat.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 5. The lyric then turns from the landscape toward the parts of a person that remain difficult to care for. Looking inward only deepens the speaker’s loneliness, and everything seems to accuse them of being at fault. That sense of blame becomes another part of their loneliness.
slides.text: The lyric then turns from the landscape toward the parts of a person that remain difficult to care for. Looking inward only deepens the speaker’s loneliness, and everything seems to accuse them of being at fault. That sense of blame becomes another part of their loneliness.

slides.altText: Slide 4 of 5. The repeated question is whether they must go on living with a self that feels like an affliction. It receives no answer. In her Genie interview, Kang Asol describes wanting to ask whether others shared this feeling. The question reaches outward even while the island remains unreachable.

decks.description: “You, Me and Namyangju” places an uncertain encounter in the snow beside a fox’s account of its present life. The speaker watches someone move away, while the ending leaves room for both contentment and thoughts of someone absent. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: Danpyunsun and the Moments Ensemble — You, Me and Namyangju

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: Danpyunsun and the Moments Ensemble — “You, Me and Namyangju”. A present life with room for memory.

Slide 2 of 4. Snow and visible breath give the encounter physical details, yet the speaker questions whether their being together is real. Repeated attention to the other person’s appearance and footsteps keeps returning to the same movement: someone is getting farther away. The lyric offers no settled explanation of what happened between them.
slides.text: Snow and visible breath give the encounter physical details, yet the speaker questions whether their being together is real. Repeated attention to the other person’s appearance and footsteps keeps returning to the same movement: someone is getting farther away. The lyric offers no settled explanation of what happened between them.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. The spoken ending shifts to a figure who says they have become a fox. Cold weather and searching the snow for insects make this new life concrete, even within its strange premise. The figure expresses satisfaction with the present, then repeatedly admits to thinking of the other person sometimes. Remembering them does not cancel that satisfaction; both feelings remain.

decks.description: “Mask Dance” takes its inspiration from Cheoyongmu, a Korean dance performed wearing Cheoyong’s mask to drive away evil spirits. Genie’s release notes describe the composition as a musical expression of the story’s strange and mysterious imagery. Music notes in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: Black String — Mask Dance

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek music notes: Black String — “Mask Dance”. A masked dance, amplified.

Slide 2 of 4. Genie’s release notes connect “Mask Dance” to Cheoyongmu and its purpose of driving away evil spirits. They also say the band combined amplifiers and effects with Korean traditional instruments to create an intense atmosphere.
slides.text: Genie’s release notes connect “Mask Dance” to Cheoyongmu and its purpose of driving away evil spirits. They also say the band combined amplifiers and effects with Korean traditional instruments to create an intense atmosphere.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. ACT’s notes describe the title track as an experiment with powerful, almost rock-like sounds, and place the band within Korean music’s long tradition of improvisation. Heo says “Mask Dance” goes furthest in that direction: the musicians create contrasts and follow one another’s accents and pitches, and beneath that interplay something emerges very close to traditional Korean forms and scales.

decks.description: In “Breath”, guitar leaves plenty of space around Yoon Mirae’s voice. The song is about the ordinary things that keep bringing back someone who is no longer there. Lyrics meaning in English, credits, background and release details.
decks.title: Yoon Mirae — Breath

slides.altText: Slide 1 of 4. indiek lyric notes: Yoon Mirae — “Breath”. Warmth that outlasts a goodbye.

Slide 2 of 4. A scarf carries the absent person into an ordinary winter day. Its colour has faded, but the warmth remains useful. The object makes memory tangible: something given in the past can still offer comfort after the relationship has changed.
slides.text: A scarf carries the absent person into an ordinary winter day. Its colour has faded, but the warmth remains useful. The object makes memory tangible: something given in the past can still offer comfort after the relationship has changed.

slides.altText: Slide 3 of 4. The speaker’s small, private smile can coexist with pain. Winter keeps bringing the other person to mind, without settling what happens next. The tenderness lies in that continued presence in daily life, where missing someone and feeling grateful for their warmth have become difficult to separate.
